messages.text:
docs: open phase 1, itos v0 in its own repository

This repository was made from the project template; phase 0 is the template's setup, inherited.
Phase 1 turns it into itos's own home: the demo app goes, the named tests become Gherkin features
at the root run by godog against the binary, verification starts after the template's squashed
commit, and the whole repository is AGPL-3.0. Its tasks are T-014 to T-019, and the registry gains
them with the two slices of scenarios.

Task: T-019

build: point the policy at itos's own layout

The template's rules were written around a demo app: src/** was the product, e2e/** its
Playwright scenarios. Here the product is the tool, so a path set names the implementation
(tools/itos/*.ts now, the Go port's packages later) and stands where src/** stood: a feat or fix
must change it or the features, a chore may not touch it, and build and ci may touch the support
tools but not it. The named tests move to features/ at the root, run by godog through go test;
-scenarios= takes a regular expression over the tags, because godog's own tag filter takes only
exact tags joined by commas, which ids_pattern cannot produce. CI gains gofmt and go vet as static
steps and the conformance corpus as a step of its own, and loses vp build, which built the demo.

Task: T-014 T-015 T-016

chore: drop the template's demo app

itos has no browser and no page. The template's demo goes: index.html, the greeting module and
its test, the scenario that opened the page, the Playwright and playwright-bdd harness and its
self-test, their dependencies, and their entries in the TypeScript, lint, audit, git-ignore and
pre-commit config. The unit coverage thresholds were the demo's, over src/**; itos is proven
through its command line, by the features and the conformance corpus, which a unit test's
coverage cannot see, so coverage is collected over the tool for the audit's scores and held to no
threshold. The pre-commit hook skips prose and feature files at features/, where they now live.

Task: T-014

build: pin Go and godog for the features

The features' steps are Go, run by godog, so that the same feature files judge the TypeScript v0
now and the Go port later. go.mod is the module github.com/donvargax/itos, with Go pinned by a
toolchain line and one dependency set, godog's. The staged Go files are formatted by gofmt and
vetted by go vet before a commit, as vp check does for the TypeScript; go vet reads packages, so
it vets the module whatever files are staged.

Task: T-015

docs: specify commits.since and the commit-msg hook's core as scenarios

The first features, @wip until a feat turns them green. since.feature is the commits.since key:
verify and the range checks start after the commit it names, without it the root commit is
checked, and config check rejects a value that is not the full SHA of a commit in the
repository. commit-msg.feature pins what the hook already does, through the command line: a
header without a type is rejected naming its rule, a sound message with its footer passes, a
footer naming an unknown task and a type touching a path it may not are rejected.
features/README.md states the rules: the black-box boundary, the ID scheme (one area per file,
ID-<AREA>-<nn>), the run and its -scenarios expression, the smoke set and the moving rule.

Task: T-016

test: run the features with godog against the binary

TestFeatures runs every *.feature file in features/ through godog, each scenario a subtest. The
steps treat itos as a black box: a scratch git repository per scenario in a temporary folder, the
binary ITOS_BIN names (tools/bin/itos by default) run in it with a clean environment, and its exit
code and output asserted. -scenarios= takes a regular expression over the tags and becomes
godog's tag filter, which itself takes only exact tags joined by commas; an expression matching
no tag fails the run, so a selection never passes by running nothing, and @wip never runs. The
smoke set starts empty, as no scenario is live yet.

Task: T-016

feat: pin the commit-msg hook's core in scenarios

The hook's core already works; these scenarios hold it through the command line, so any
implementation must keep it: a header without a type is rejected and the output names the rule
(type-empty, from the header lint the config delegates to), a sound chore message with its Task:
footer passes, a footer naming a task the ledger lacks is rejected by the task-footer rule, and a
docs commit staging a path outside prose is rejected naming the path. The footer cases run with
no delegate, so the footer rules judged are itos's own. The smoke set takes the unknown-task case.

Scenarios: @ID-CMSG-01 @ID-CMSG-02 @ID-CMSG-03 @ID-CMSG-04

feat: start verification at commits.since

A repository made from a GitHub template begins with one squashed commit no rule passes, and a
project adopting itos has a history written before its rules; CI verifies everything after its
last green run, so with no green run yet it judged that history on every push. commits.since in
itos.yaml names the commit where verification starts: verify leaves it and its ancestors out and
says so, and the range checks start there, at it when the range's own start is empty or older.
A since that is not a full SHA is a config error; one the repository does not have fails
config check and verify with exit 2, as a config error does, since a shortened SHA can grow
ambiguous and a branch can move. The commit-msg hook, which judges one commit, is unchanged.
Without the key everything is checked as before. The conformance corpus gains the cases.

Scenarios: @ID-SINCE-01 @ID-SINCE-02 @ID-SINCE-03 @ID-SINCE-04 @ID-SINCE-05 @ID-SINCE-06

build: start verification after the template's squashed commit

GitHub made this repository from the project template as one squashed commit, "Initial commit",
which no rule passes: it is not a Conventional Commit, and it adds a live scenario outside feat
and fix. CI verifies every commit after the last green run, and there has been none, so every push
was red. commits.since now names that commit, and verify and the scenario-move check start after
it.

Task: T-017

test: prove the gates and the features' selection on itos itself

The gates self-test drove the demo app: a greeting module, a page heading every scenario read, a
coverage threshold. It now proves the same on itos: a change to a leaf module runs only its
unit test on both hooks and fails there when it breaks it, the commit-msg shim rejects a docs
commit touching itos and a renamed live scenario, and a refactor that changes what verify prints,
in a module no unit test imports, passes both hooks and fails the push's features step, whose
smoke set reads that line. The features-scope self-test replaces the Playwright one: go test's own
record of what it ran shows that the smoke run, a range naming a scenario, the whole run and a
range naming tasks select exactly what the plan claims, in one run. The conformance corpus leaves
the unit suite, as it is now a CI step of its own and would otherwise run twice.

Task: T-014 T-016

ci: set Go up and drop Playwright from the workflows

Both workflows set Go up from go.mod, whose toolchain line pins the version, for the features'
steps; neither installs a browser or uploads Playwright's report any more, and the scope step
that only decided whether to install the browser goes. The nightly's red issue lists the failing
scenarios from go test's `--- FAIL: TestFeatures/…` lines, as it listed Playwright's.

Task: T-014 T-015

chore: license the whole repository under AGPL-3.0

The template is 0BSD, so a project made from it owes nothing, and carries the task tool under its
own AGPL-3.0 licence in tools/itos/. This repository is the tool, so the whole of it is AGPL-3.0:
the root LICENSE takes that text and the folder's copy goes.

Task: T-018

ci: name the nightly's job after what it runs

The job was named e2e after the template's Playwright suite; it runs every feature and then the
gates self-test, so it is the nightly.

Task: T-014

docs: describe itos, not the template's demo

README.md and PLAN.md were the template's: a demo app and a skeleton. README now says what itos
is (the name, and how it differs from withakay/ito), its two halves (itos for the rules a command
can decide, the agent instructions for the rest) and its status (v0 in TypeScript, the Go port
next, judged by the same features). PLAN.md carries the plan for itos in this repository's terms:
the goals and non-goals, the decisions, the model, the schema, the command line, the layout, the
phases and the distribution, each reason stated in general. AGENTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md,
docs/ORCHESTRATING.md, docs/PHASES.md and tasks/README.md describe the features, the godog run,
the implementation path set and the gates as they now are, not e2e/, Playwright or src/; the
contributors' links point here.

Task: T-019

docs: fit phase 0's checks to this repository

Phase 0 is the template's setup, inherited and done, but several of its checks ran the demo app
phase 1 removed: the page's build, its Playwright scenario and self-test, a scope check against
src/greeting.ts, the 0BSD licence. Each task keeps its subject and now checks what holds here:
the Go module beside vp install, the features and their self-test for the named tests, the
implementation path set in the commit rules, AGPL-3.0; each why says what changed and where.

Task: T-014 T-016 T-018

docs: close phase 1's tasks and record what v0 leaves open

T-014 to T-019 and the two slices are done. What remains goes into the registry as ideas: the
v0.1.0 release packed to JavaScript, CI verifying with the last release, config check in a gate,
the config keys validated but not read, one defaults table, the footer rules beside the header
lint rather than inside its plugin, more than one kind of named test, the template's E2E names
left in the code, a range check given commits.since when a range has diverged from it, and the
hook, identity, provider and agent-rule ideas carried from the plan; phase 2, the Go port, opens
with its own.

Task: T-019

docs: write the first handoff: release v0.1.0, then a clean config, then the port

The template's placeholder becomes what the next session acts on: where itos stands, its two
consumers waiting on a release, and the next steps in order. The coverage threshold that left with
the demo app waits on the user.

docs: specify the v0.1.0 release as two tasks, the tarball and the release

The release idea becomes T-020 (build: vp pack bundles itos into one JavaScript entry point,
proven by installing the tarball offline and running the corpus and every feature against it)
and T-021 (ci: a v* tag publishes the tarball and checksums.txt as a GitHub release). Split so
the packing lands and is proven before anything is published. Both are taken, and the
verify-with-last-release idea now waits on T-021.

Task: T-020, T-021

build: pack itos to one JavaScript file, and prove the tarball it installs

A consumer pins itos as a dependency, and Node strips types only outside node_modules, so
tools/itos/*.ts cannot run from an install. vite.config.ts gains a `pack` block: vp pack bundles
tools/itos/main.ts and everything it imports, yaml and the commands' lazy imports included, into
dist/itos.mjs with a node shebang. package.json names it as the `itos` bin, lists it with LICENSE
and README.md as the package's files, and takes version 0.1.0, as tools/itos/version.ts says, so
npm pack gives itos-0.1.0.tgz with no runtime dependencies. Nothing in the source reads a file
beside itself, so the bundle needed no change to it. tools/bin/itos still runs the working tree's
TypeScript, which the hooks and CI judge.

tools/selftest/release.ts proves the tarball rather than the source: it packs (or takes
--tarball, the one a release publishes), installs it offline into a scratch project with an empty
npm cache, requires that project to hold itos and nothing else and the installed bin to report
package.json's version, then runs the conformance corpus and every feature against that bin.
Against a bundle that left yaml out it failed on all three.

Task: T-020

docs: record the package and the release self-test, and close T-020

ARCHITECTURE.md says how the package is put together (the pack block, the one bundled file, the
bin and files of package.json, tools/bin/itos still running the TypeScript here) and what
tools/selftest/release.ts proves. T-020's why records what its check found: the source reads no
file beside itself, so the bundle needed nothing from it, and a bundle without yaml fails the
self-test. T-020 is done in the work registry.

Task: T-020

docs: run T-021's release check last, after what the push proves

The check that downloads v0.1.0 and verifies its checksum can pass only once the tag's release
exists, and CI runs it on every range that names T-021, before the tag as well. As a static
check it ran first and, failing, stopped the run before the unit suite, the corpus, the features
and T-020's checks, so a red run before the release proved nothing. Without cost: static it is
late, like T-008's check of CI's own result: the run that lands the release workflow proves
everything else before failing there, the tag goes on that commit, and the run is green re-run
after the release. The check still runs, and must pass, on every such range.

Task: T-021

ci: release a v* tag as its tarball and checksum

Consumers pin a release, never a branch. release.yml runs on a v* tag: it packs (vp pack, then
npm pack), refuses a tag other than v<package.json's version> and a packed itos whose `itos
version` names another, runs tools/selftest/release.ts against the very tarball it will publish
(installed offline, the corpus and every feature against its bin), writes checksums.txt with
sha256sum, and publishes a GitHub release of the two, its notes quoting the checksum. The
actions are pinned as ci.yml pins them; the job alone may write contents. The version is checked
with `itos version`, the command itos has for it: there is no --version flag.

Task: T-021

docs: say how a consumer installs a pinned release

The README gains an Install section: a release holds itos-<version>.tgz and checksums.txt; a
consumer checks the tarball against the listed SHA-256 once, then depends on the tarball's
release URL, so package.json pins the URL and the lockfile its integrity, and a replaced release
fails every later install.

Task: T-021

docs: close T-021 with v0.1.0 released, and record what the release leaves open

v0.1.0 is released: the tag's workflow proved itos-0.1.0.tgz installed offline against the corpus
and every feature and published it with checksums.txt, and T-021's check downloads both and
verifies the hash. T-021 is done in the work registry.

Two gaps go in as ideas. The tarball carries the repository's package.json, whose prepare
script npm lists on every consumer's install and which declares no engines though the bundle
needs Node 24. And CI fails a named task's after-push check that only a later tag can satisfy,
so the push that landed the release workflow was red until the release existed.

Task: T-021

docs: specify config check in the gates as T-022

No hook ran itos config check, and CI only when a pushed commit named a task carrying it, so a
broken config, ledger, registry or smoke set could land and fail someone else's later push. T-022
makes it a static CI step, a prose step (the registry is under docs/**), and a pre-commit step when
the files it reads are staged, proven by a self-test that a broken ledger is rejected.

Task: T-022

docs: specify slices 3 and 4, every config key itos accepts is one it reads

The config-keys audit found keys the loader validates and no tool reads, and commands run through
sh -c whatever shell says. features/config.feature specifies the fix, all @wip: slice 3 runs every
command itos starts through the configured shell and reads ci.stop_at_first_failure; slice 4 reads
work.statuses, work.groups_key, smoke.every_file and hooks.manager, and drops the keys of features
not built yet (commits.header_lint.use and alongside, ledger.check.pushed), which return with them.
The names the tools still hardcode stay an idea, after slice 4.

ci: run itos config check in the pre-commit hook and in every CI plan

No hook ran `itos config check`, and CI only when a pushed commit named a task carrying it, so a
broken config, ledger, registry or smoke set could land and fail a later push. It is now a static
step of `ci.steps`, beside the smoke check, and one of `ci.prose.steps`, since
docs/work-items.yaml is under docs/** and a prose-only push can break the registry. The
pre-commit hook runs it when itos.yaml, tasks/, docs/work-items.yaml or features/smoke.yaml is
staged, before the prose exit that skips tasks/, so every other commit costs what it did.

tools/selftest/config-gate.ts proves both in a scratch worktree: the hook rejects a commit
staging a ledger with a misspelt key and passes a sound one, and `itos ci plan` runs the check
for a prose-only range touching the registry and for one touching the ledger. Run before the
gate was added, it failed all three.

The scratch worktree it builds is the one gates.ts built, so that code moved to
tools/selftest/scratch.ts and both self-tests (and release.ts, for the hook-free environment) take
it from there, rather than keeping a copy each.

Task: T-022

docs: close T-022, with config check in the gates, and record what it leaves open

AGENTS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md now say the pre-commit hook runs `itos config check` when the
config, the ledger, the registry or the smoke set is staged, and that CI runs it as a static step
and a prose step; AGENTS.md drops it from what no gate does. The new self-test and the shared
scratch worktree join the architecture's self-tests.

The registry marks T-022 done and adds p1-config-check-staged: the hook's check reads the working
tree, not the index, so a ledger staged broken and fixed only on disk passes it until the push.

Task: T-022

docs: two orchestration lessons from the v0.1.0 release and T-022

A check only a later act can satisfy (T-021's, waiting on the release) fails every push that
names its task until then, so it is written late and the pushes before it are expected red at that
one check. And the rtk hook's rewrite of git pull can refuse a rebase that rtk proxy runs as
written, which T-022's agent met.

docs: take slice 3, every command through the configured shell

Slice 3 is started: checks, CI steps, the header-lint delegates and range checks go through the
shell the config names, and ci.stop_at_first_failure is read. Marking it doing keeps another
session from building the same thing.

feat: start every command through the configured shell, and read ci.stop_at_first_failure

shell was validated and printed among the defaults, but only the providers and the command adapter
honoured it: task checks, CI steps, the header-lint delegates, the range checks, the pre-push
commands and the smoke run started sh -c whatever it said, so a project on another shell (Windows,
say) got a key that changed nothing. They now all start through one function, shell.ts's inShell,
which reads shell as the providers did; the smoke run quotes its extra arguments into the command
instead of passing them as sh's positional ones, which only sh -c understands.

ci.stop_at_first_failure was validated and never read. With it false, ci run runs every step and
check of the plan, prints "CI failed at: ..." for each that fails, and exits with the first
failure's code, which --json's failed_at names; unknown tasks still end the run first, since they
name nothing to run. The default stays true, and --print-defaults now lists it.

A push's plan read the smoke set of the kind named scenario even when no ci step runs named tests,
so a CI of plain steps failed with "tests.scenario is missing" before running any. The plan (and
ci plan --data-at) now reads the smoke set of the kind its tests step names, and none without one.

The conformance corpus gains the cases: every step and check run when the key is false, its --json,
a CI with no tests step, and a step and a check through a shell that announces them. ci run's help
says what the key does, and its case changes with it. config.feature's smoke entry is
@ID-CONFIG-01, the quickest command that goes through the shell.

Scenarios: @ID-CONFIG-01 @ID-CONFIG-02 @ID-CONFIG-03 @ID-CONFIG-04 @ID-CONFIG-05 @ID-CONFIG-06

docs: close slice 3, every command through the configured shell, and record what it leaves open

The architecture says how commands now start (shell.ts, one function that reads shell), that the
plan reads the smoke set of its tests step's kind, and what ci.stop_at_first_failure: false does;
the plan's command table and tasks/README.md say it too. slice-3 is done.

Three gaps go in the registry as ideas: an empty shell is accepted and breaks every command, ci run
--json names only the first failure when it goes on past it, and vp run changelog fails on the
template's unconventional first commit, which git-cliff gives no footers. The config-names idea
drops ci plan --data-at, which now reads the tests step's kind.

docs: specify v0.2.0, the registry beside the ledger and itos's data checked at commit

itos's consumers asked for two changes before they move their pin. Slice 5: the work registry's
default home becomes tasks/work-items.yaml, beside the ledger, with work.registry still overriding
it (features/work.feature). Slice 6: the commit-msg hook validates itos.yaml, the ledger, the
registry and the smoke set from the staged tree, since a project's pre-commit hook passes them as
prose (features/commit-data.feature); it closes the staged-tree gap T-022 left, so that idea goes.
T-023 then drops the pre-commit hook's own config check, and T-024 releases v0.2.0 with the
version in one place. Slice 4 waits for v0.3.0: it drops keys a consumer's config may still set.
@ID-CONFIG-07 expected work check's exit 2; it exits 1 on a problem.

Task: T-023, T-024

docs: take slice 5, the registry beside the ledger, and specify its move as T-025

Slice 5 is started: the registry's default home becomes tasks/work-items.yaml. Marking it doing
keeps another session from building the same thing.

Moving this repository's own registry is T-025, a chore: the file and itos.yaml's work.registry
line must move in one commit, or the tree between them fails config check, and no docs or ci
commit may touch both tasks/** and itos.yaml. Its checks are the registry sound where itos now
looks, nothing left at the old path, and the config gate's self-test, which the move changes.
slice-5 waits on it.

Task: T-025

feat: read the work registry at tasks/work-items.yaml by default, and say so when it is not there

The registry is itos's data, like the ledger, and read every day, so its default home is now
beside the ledger, tasks/work-items.yaml, leaving docs/ for prose; work.registry still puts it
anywhere else. The default is one constant in config.ts that the loader, the plan, ci plan
--data-at and the defaults table config check --print-defaults prints all read, where each wrote
docs/work-items.yaml for itself.

With no file where itos looks, work check, work and config check's registry part failed with
Node's ENOENT and exit 2. Each now reports the problem work-registry-missing, "no work registry at
<path>", exit 1, with a fix: move the registry there or set work.registry. A project that kept its
registry at the old default learns on its first run of v0.2.0 where itos reads it now. ci run's
line for a task not started named docs/work-items.yaml whatever the config said; it names the
registry the plan read.

The conformance corpus records the new default in the two --print-defaults cases and work check's
help, and gains the default read without work.registry, the missing registry for work check (text
and --json), work, an explicit file and config check. The features' scratch repositories start
with their registry at the default; work.feature's smoke entry is @ID-WORK-01.

Scenarios: @ID-WORK-01 @ID-WORK-02 @ID-WORK-03

chore: move this repository's work registry to tasks/work-items.yaml, its default home

itos now reads the registry at tasks/work-items.yaml unless work.registry says otherwise, so this
repository's registry moves there with git mv and itos.yaml's work.registry line goes. They move
in one commit because either half alone leaves a tree whose config check fails, and only a chore
may touch both tasks/** and itos.yaml.

What named the old path in passing follows it. The pre-commit hook's config-check paths drop it,
since tasks covers the registry now, and a commit staging only the registry passes the prose exit
as the ledger does. The identity fixture reads the registry at the default. The prose steps'
config check stays: a prose-only edit to CONTRIBUTORS.md can still break the registry, whose owners
must be among the people. The config gate's self-test proves that and that a range touching only
the registry is not prose and runs the check, where it proved a prose-only range touching
docs/work-items.yaml did. The conformance cases whose scratch projects mirror this layout (the plan,
ci run, the docs scope) put their registry at tasks/work-items.yaml.

Task: T-025

docs: close slice 5, the registry beside the ledger, and record what it leaves open

The registry is at tasks/work-items.yaml now, so every page that named docs/work-items.yaml names
it: AGENTS.md, PLAN.md, the architecture, the phases, orchestration, the READMEs, CONTRIBUTORS.md
and tasks/README.md. PLAN.md records the decision and the default in the model. The architecture
says the registry is not a ledger file, the pre-commit hook's config check covers it through
tasks/, and the prose steps keep config check because CONTRIBUTORS.md, the people the registry's
owners must be among, is Markdown. T-022's why says the same. slice-5 and T-025 are done.

Two gaps go in the registry as ideas. A ledger.files of tasks/{group}.yaml with the default group
pattern matches tasks/work-items.yaml and reads the registry as a ledger file. And a staged people
file can break the registry, which slice 6 checks at commit only when the registry itself is
staged. The defaults-table and config-names ideas drop what this slice settled: the registry's
fallback is one constant now, and ci run names the registry it read.

Task: T-025

report: ⚠   footer must have leading blank line [footer-leading-blank]
⚠   footer must have leading blank line [footer-leading-blank]

messages.text:
docs: keep task checks independent of the index, before the hook runs them

Slice 7 has the commit-msg hook run the static checks of the tasks a commit names while the commit
is being made. Two of T-007's checks ran the hook itself on "build: x" and "docs: x", judging
whatever was staged: in CI the index is empty and both held, but mid-commit "docs: x" fails as soon
as anything beyond prose is staged, which would reject a correct commit naming T-007. The
commit-msg scenarios prove the same hook in repositories the steps build, so T-007 runs them
instead. verify "" HEAD (T-008, T-017) is sized by the history and becomes late, so the hook stops
before it. tasks/README.md states the rule they broke.

Task: T-007

docs: specify slice 7, the commit-msg hook runs the named tasks' static checks, and T-026

A commit that breaks a finished task should be stopped before it is made, not found by CI.
features/commit-tasks.feature specifies it, all @wip: the hook runs the static checks of the tasks
the Task: footer names, in written order up to the first late one; a failure rejects the commit
when the task's work item is done, and for a task in progress, or with no item, prints its status
and lets the commit through, since a task is committed in steps and CI judges what is pushed.
hooks.commit_msg.task_checks turns it off and hooks.commit_msg.check_timeout caps each check. It
ships after v0.2.0, so the release the consumers wait for is not held up. T-026: the docs call
tools/bin/itos task directly and the package.json script goes, one name for one command.

Task: T-026

docs: take slice 6, itos's own data checked by the commit-msg hook as staged

slice-6 goes to doing: the commit-msg hook will validate itos.yaml, the ledger, the work registry
and the smoke set from the staged tree, and reject the commit with their problems.

feat: check itos's own data in the commit-msg hook, as staged

A project's pre-commit hook passes itos.yaml, the ledger, the work registry and the smoke set as
prose, and T-022's own pre-commit check read them from the working tree, which can hold what the
commit does not. itos hook commit-msg now validates them itself: when the commit stages the config,
a ledger file, the registry or a smoke set (as the staged config names them), it runs itos config
check's problems over the staged tree and rejects the commit with them, one a line under the
reject message, exit 1. The registry's own check is part of that one. A commit staging none of them
runs no check, and the rule comes first, since the hook's other rules read the config.

The data's readers (the config loader, the ledger, the registry, the people, the smoke sets and the
smoke rule's live scenarios) read through one source, source.ts: the working tree by default, or
for as long as a function runs a tree git holds, the index or a commit, the way ci plan --data-at
reads a commit. So config check and the hook's check are the same code. A config the index does not
hold (an ITOS_CONFIG outside the repository) is read where it is; anything else the index lacks is
a problem, such as a registry staged while its people file is untracked.

The conformance corpus gains the staged ledger, registry and itos.yaml rejected while the working
tree's copy is sound, staged data that cannot be read, and a commit staging none of it left
unchecked; the hook's help says what it runs first, and its case changes with it.
commit-data.feature's smoke entry is @ID-CDATA-01, a rejection with the problem.
